clue.text: Commonly, mad-naturally, always being brought up by strangers!

definitions.meaning: in everyday slang someone crazy is said to be loopy or nuts in this sense

definitions.text: naturally, always being brought up by strangers
definitions.meaning: a bird species that lays its eggs in other birds' nests, so its young are reared by foster parents

explanation.surface: An exclamation about someone odd who was raised by people not their own.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal slang for crazy, and also names the bird famous for leaving its chicks to be reared by other species.

clue.text: Used for restrictive practices a hundred times

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
ages means long periods or eras, i.e. times

explanation.surface: Something employed for restrictive working practices on a hundred occasions.
explanation.definitionFit: Enclosures with bars are used to confine animals, a literal restrictive practice.

clue.text: Made at a meet!

parts.note: when people meet, connection or touch is made; the exclamation marks the whimsical reading

explanation.surface: Something achieved at a hunting meet or gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: You make touch or connection with someone when you meet them, as in 'make the acquaintance'.

clue.text: Eatable Spanish spring may accompany it

definitions.text: Eatable Spanish spring may accompany it

parts.words: Eatable Spanish spring may accompany it
parts.note: both Spanish and spring are adjectives naming varieties of one common edible bulb

explanation.surface: A Spanish spring season might go along with something edible.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish and spring are both kinds of this pungent vegetable bulb used in cooking.

clue.text: Fix the ship

parts.note: to hold a vessel fast in one place by dropping a heavy hook to the seabed

explanation.surface: An order to repair the vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' looks like repair, but here it means to hold in position.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropping a heavy hooked weight is how a vessel is held fixed in place at sea.

clue.text: Lack of belief quite spoiled his meat

indicators.note: meat that is spoiled has gone bad, signalling these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone without faith complains that his meat has gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: Disbelief in any god is the absence of religious faith.

clue.text: Calling to one coming down hard!

definitions.meaning: shouting a greeting to somebody to attract notice
falling as frozen pellets from the sky

explanation.surface: Shouting at somebody while heavy weather falls.
explanation.definitionFit: To hail a cab is to call to it; hail is also ice pellets that fall from clouds.

clue.text: Puts things right concerning some outfits

parts.note: re is a business-letter word for about or concerning
dresses are garments, outfits for women

explanation.surface: A tailor corrects matters relating to a few outfits.
explanation.definitionFit: To remedy a wrong or set a grievance right is to correct it.

clue.text: Book blown away

definitions.meaning: a famous novel by Margaret Mitchell set in the American Civil War
carried off by a strong gust of air

explanation.surface: A book that has been carried off by a gale.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Mitchell's novel title literally describes something carried off by a gale.

clue.text: Pancho messes about our own places

indicators.note: the run of letters lies about, that is within, the two words

explanation.surface: A man named Pancho makes a mess around our houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messes about' looks like the anagram signal, but the letters run on unchanged across 'PancHO MESses'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwellings where people live are the places they belong to.

clue.text: Names a strange kind of traveller

indicators.note: strange means odd or altered, signalling the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone lists a peculiar type of voyager.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor travels the oceans for a living.

clue.text: A sort of way through stone

parts.note: a gate is an opening in a fence, a way through

explanation.surface: A kind of passage through rock.
explanation.definitionFit: This banded form of chalcedony is a semi-precious gemstone.

clue.text: Suggests a course over water carrying most passengers

definitions.text: Suggests a course over water carrying most passengers

parts.words: Suggests a course over water carrying most passengers
parts.note: the first word suggests the sea, the second a course; together they are the principal railway route carrying the bulk of travellers

explanation.surface: A ferry route that carries the bulk of the passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk railway route between major cities carries the greatest number of travellers; main is also a poetic word for the sea.

clue.text: Act so? Get wrong living quarters, then

indicators.note: getting something wrong muddles it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor told to behave this way gets it wrong, and so ends up in lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges ACTSO and GET together; 'then' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Small country houses are places where people live.

clue.text: Holy man who owns up, it seems

definitions.text: Holy man who owns up, it seems

parts.words: Holy man who owns up, it seems
parts.note: the word looks like one who admits things, yet it is also a priest who hears admissions or a saintly king

explanation.surface: A clergyman who apparently admits his guilt.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a priest hearing admissions of sin, though literally it looks like someone owning up.

clue.text: More than one little beast digs me out

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A creature tunnels and excavates the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: These tiny biting flies are small creatures, plural.

clue.text: Aim wrongly-up, for example — to get the idol

indicators.note: doing something wrongly scrambles it, so the letters are rearranged
in a down entry, up means the piece is read from bottom to top

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Someone aims badly, for instance, and ends up with an idol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges AIM into IMA; 'up' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue worshipped as a god is a graven likeness.

clue.text: Revolutionary gang of the French constantly found fault

indicators.note: revolutionary means overturning, signalling the letters are mixed up

parts.note: de is French for of

explanation.surface: A rebel band of Frenchmen kept complaining.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep scolding someone persistently is to carp at them.

clue.text: Broken legs can get looks!

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, signalling these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fractured limbs attract stares.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick peeks are brief looks.

clue.text: Get less to do it

parts.note: to shrink gradually is the action of becoming smaller in amount

explanation.surface: An instruction to reduce effort in doing a task.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish steadily is to grow smaller or fewer.

clue.text: Massive buildings are pointed out on the sand!

definitions.text: Massive buildings are pointed out on the sand!

parts.words: Massive buildings are pointed out on the sand!
parts.note: huge pointed monuments standing in the Egyptian desert, with a pun on pointed

explanation.surface: Tour guides indicate huge structures on a beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointed out' seems to mean indicated, but the buildings themselves come to a point.
explanation.definitionFit: The great pointed tombs of Egypt are vast structures in the desert.

clue.text: One without a religion is quiet again when I leave

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quiet

indicators.note: when the letter I leaves the word, it is taken out

explanation.surface: A heathen goes quiet once more after the speaker departs.
explanation.definitionFit: A heathen holds no mainstream faith.

clue.text: It's time to go-quickly!

parts.note: a moment of time, and also an adjective meaning immediate or fast

explanation.surface: A hurried announcement that it is time to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for a moment and an adjective for something immediate.

clue.text: Getting things out of people is demanding work

definitions.meaning: extracting money or obedience from others

explanation.surface: Extracting things from people is hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' and 'work' only join the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact is to extract by demand, and an arduous task is called this.

clue.text: Treated someone plaguily!

parts.note: plaguily is a coined adverb from plague in the sense of pester; to have pestered someone playfully

explanation.surface: Someone dealt with another person in a pestilent way.
explanation.definitionFit: To plague in the mild sense is to tease or pester someone.

clue.text: Also, a pound a point for the instruments

parts.note: too means also
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra
S is a compass point, south

explanation.surface: In addition, the instruments cost a pound each.
explanation.definitionFit: Implements used for working are instruments.

clue.text: A trick to take steps to avoid!

definitions.meaning: to step aside quickly to escape something

explanation.surface: A ruse for sidestepping trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a cunning ruse, and to dodge is to evade by moving aside.

clue.text: Ringside chap having authority? No, one is above him

definitions.text: Ringside chap having authority? No, one is above him

parts.words: Ringside chap having authority? No, one is above him
parts.note: a boxer's ringside attendant combined with holding power, describing a deputy who has a superior

explanation.surface: A boxer's helper seems in charge, but someone outranks him.
explanation.walkthrough: A second is a boxer's attendant at the ringside.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy holds authority but ranks just below the chief.

clue.text: Having started, must stop to be able to do this

definitions.text: Having started, must stop to be able to do this

parts.words: Having started, must stop to be able to do this
parts.note: you can only carry on again after something has begun and then paused

explanation.surface: A rule that one must halt something begun before doing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To restart after an interruption you must first have begun and then paused.

clue.text: Went hard for the golfer, offering an inside sit-down!

parts.note: jelly or concrete that has set has gone hard
a tee is the peg a golfer places the ball on

explanation.surface: Something solidified for a golfer offering an indoor seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa is an indoor seat for sitting down on.
